content.quote: Everyone knows Wuthering Heights. Everyone knows Jane Eyre. This is a play about the Brontë sister you can't quite name — and about what her family did to make sure of that.

content.headline: Three sisters. Three pen names.
content.body: Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell: Charlotte, Emily and Anne published as men, keeping their initials.

content.headline: Two novels. An uncompromising voice.
content.body: Anne wrote Agnes Grey (1847) and The Tenant of Wildfell Hall (1848). Her second novel was a hit.

content.headline: A sister's verdict
content.body: After Anne died, Charlotte opposed a new edition of The Tenant of Wildfell Hall. It remained out of print for years.

content.headline: The {other} other one
content.body: Anne died in Scarborough in 1849, aged 29. Her writing still asks difficult questions.

content.headline: Not just a bonnet drama
content.body: “The Brontës meets Fleabag”: the Nick Darke Award judges on Sarah Gordon's prize-winning script, 2020.
